list.snippet: UL 2218 Standard: Rated to survive a 2-inch steel ball dropped from 20 feet in a laboratory test without cracking or rupturing on the backside.
Construction: Built with SBS-modified (polymer-modified) asphalt that gives the shingle a rubber-like flexibility to absorb the impact of hail and debris rather than shattering.
Cost vs. Standard: Typically costs 10% to 25% more than standard architectural shingles (roughly $3.75 to $5.00+ per square foot installed, depending on the material).

Insurance Discounts: Many insurance carriers in Utah offer policy discounts for Class 4 impact-resistant roofs, though discounts are not automatic . Check with your specific insurance provider before installing to confirm what documentation or rating they require.
Climate Fit: Ideal for parts of Utah prone to severe summer hail or heavy seasonal temperature swings that cause standard asphalt to become brittle over time.
Local Guidance: Review local options and learn more about regional roof performance via Superior Home Improvement or research local climate considerations through Frame Restoration Utah .
